title: What Is Gratitude? A Qualitative Analysis of Gratitude for a Culturally Sensitive Understanding With Brazilians
abstract: Research on gratitude, conducted mainly in the Global North, may not adequately capture the nuances of the phenomenon in other cultures. This qualitative study investigated the manifestations and meanings of gratitude in a group of Brazilian adults. Through semi-structured interviews with 19 participants, content analysis revealed that gratitude is a multidimensional phenomenon, encompassing emotional, cognitive-reflective, behavioural, social-relational, and existential/transcendental facets. Participants situated gratitude collectively and existentially, addressing it not only to benefactors and the divine but also to life, nature, and society, and experienced it in adversity as a way of reframing loss. In some accounts gratitude arose in the act of giving rather than in receiving a benefit. Its opposite was described not as the mere absence of gratitude but as a distinct phenomenon, encompassing indifference, rejection, and failures of empathy with their own relational costs. These findings underscore the need for theoretical models that incorporate a culturally sensitive perspective, capable of capturing the complexity of gratitude in diverse social contexts.
